articles.title: The late-night habit Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld picked up since welcoming baby Harper is adorably nerdy
articles.summary: NFL News: Josh Allen is not sitting up at 3 a.m. watching game film right now. The Buffalo Bills quarterback is doing something far more unexpected during those.
articles.body: Josh Allen is not sitting up at 3 a.m. watching game film right now. The Buffalo Bills quarterback is doing something far more unexpected during those groggy windows between baby feedings and Hailee Steinfeld is right there alongside him. In an August 28 interview with Adam Schein on Mad Dog Sports Radio, Allen revealed that he and his wife have quietly built a nightly routine that involves the New York Times puzzle suite. No TV. No doom-scrolling. Just Wordle, Connections, and the crossword.What does Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld do during late-night baby feedings?The couple welcomed their daughter, Harper Haize Allen, in April. At four months old, Harper is at the stage where she tracks the TV screen if it's on, which apparently made the decision for Allen and Steinfeld pretty simple. Allen told Schein they are limiting screen time around the baby, so the television stays off during those middle-of-the-night stretches.That left them with options. They landed on the NYT games. Every night, the two of them work through the crossword, Connections, and Wordle together. For a couple navigating the fog of new parenthood, it is the kind of low-key ritual that keeps them present with each other without requiring much energy. It also, clearly, suits both of them.The detail that gives the whole story its texture, though, is the Wordle starter. Allen does not just open the app and pick a random word. He always opens with the same one: "harps." The nod to his daughter's first name -- Harper, Harp, Harps -- is subtle enough to feel like a private thing, which is probably exactly what it is. A small, daily ritual inside a larger one.Josh Allen has been open about how fatherhood has shifted his perspective heading into his ninth NFL season. Earlier this month on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show, he described becoming a "little softer" since Harper arrived, saying fatherhood makes your heart grow bigger and puts things in the world in a different light. He also connected it to his approach on the field, suggesting that hearing people out and navigating different opinions will come more naturally to him now.Steinfeld, who recently appeared in the film Sinners, announced Harper's arrival through her newsletter, Beau Society, back in April. She followed it up in June with a letter addressed to her daughter, written on the occasion of her first Mother's Day. In it, she wrote: "I'm in awe of you. You've been here for only a short while now, and somehow it feels as though you've always been ours." She also added, with a measure of humor, that Allen is now outnumbered on movie night.Allen and Steinfeld married in May 2025. The Bills open their 2026-2027 regular season on September 13 against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium. Harper, presumably, will be watching -- screens or not.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Travis Kelce is already building a $90 million post-NFL empire before his likely final season ends
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce has not officially retired yet, but the business decisions he is making right now look a lot like someone who already has one eye on life.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has not officially retired yet, but the business decisions he is making right now look a lot like someone who already has one eye on life after football. Just weeks into what many expect to be his final NFL season, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end launched Tekta, a new NIL consulting agency built in partnership with French advertising giant Publicis Groupe. That announcement, dropped on August 18, was not a celebrity vanity project. It was the latest move in a financial portfolio that already sits between $90 million and $100 million.What is Tekta and why did Travis Kelce launch it now?Tekta is not just another celebrity endorsement deal. The agency is designed to connect brands with college athletes through NIL agreements, giving companies access to a network of 45,000 Division I student-athletes across 68 Power Four universities. Kelce serves as an adviser, while his talent firm, 3 Arts Sports, operates as the strategic partner on the ground.The timing matters. Kelce is 36 years old and playing through what many insiders believe is his last season in the league. Signing a three-year deal worth up to $57.7 million in March 2026 bought him one more year on the field, but the activity happening off it tells a sharper story. Tekta gives Kelce a real stake in the NIL economy, an industry that barely existed when he was in college at Cincinnati and is now generating billions annually.For brands, the pitch is specific. Publicis Sports brings advertiser relationships, fan intelligence, and measurement tools. Kelce brings credibility and a face that people outside the NFL still recognize. That combination is not easy to replicate, and Kelce clearly understands his own shelf life as an active athlete well enough to lock in partnerships before he stops playing.How much does Travis Kelce actually make off the field?His Chiefs contract pays him around $17 million a year. His podcast pays him more than that. In August 2024, Travis and Jason Kelce signed a three-year deal with Amazon's Wondery podcast platform reportedly valued at $100 million in total, with Travis's estimated share running to roughly $16 to $17 million annually -- which already matches or exceeds what the Chiefs wire to his account each season.Then layer on the endorsement side. Kelce earns an estimated $30 to $32 million per year from brand deals, a number that nearly doubled after his relationship with Taylor Swift became public in 2023. His investment portfolio includes Cholula hot sauce, Hydrow rowing machines, Indochino, RealTruck, and ThePlayersTV. He acquired Garage Beer in 2024, holds a stake in Six Flags, and has his own clothing line, Tru Kolors, and a nutrition brand called Hilo. Twelve known investments in total.When you add it all up, Kelce pulls in roughly $50 million a year across football, podcasting, and endorsements, with his overall net worth sitting at $90 million by most credible estimates. None of those numbers include what marriage into a $1.8 billion fortune might do for his brand reach going forward.What happens to Travis Kelce's business empire after he retires from the NFL?Most athletes spend their post-playing years figuring out what comes next. Kelce has spent his playing years making sure he never has to wonder. The New Heights podcast does not need him in a Chiefs uniform to hold its audience. The endorsement deals tied to his personality rather than his position will not evaporate the moment he retires. And Tekta, the newest piece of the puzzle, is built on a market that is only getting bigger.What makes the Kelce business model different from the average athlete-turned-entrepreneur is that he has not bet on one category. He has spread across media, consumer goods, performance products, entertainment, and now the college sports economy. Each piece feeds the others. The podcast keeps his name in people's ears. The endorsement deals keep his face in front of brands. Tekta puts him inside conversations that happen at the agency and boardroom level.At 36, with one foot already pointed toward the exit, Kelce is not scrambling to build something. He is managing what is already there. By the time the final whistle blows on his NFL career, the business side will not skip a beat.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How one $100,000 check from Travis Kelce told you everything you need to know about who he really is
articles.summary: NFL News: When two young girls were shot at the Kansas City Chiefs' Super Bowl victory parade in February 2024, the world watched in horror. Twenty-two people w.
articles.body: When two young girls were shot at the Kansas City Chiefs' Super Bowl victory parade in February 2024, the world watched in horror. Twenty-two people were injured. One woman died. While most celebrities responded with social media posts, Travis Kelce did something different. His foundation, Eighty-Seven and Running, sent two separate $50,000 checks to the Reyes family before the news cycle had even moved on. No press conference. No announcement. Just the money.How did Travis Kelce help the victims of the Chiefs parade shooting?The shooting on February 14, 2024, left the city shattered. Among the wounded were two young sisters from the Reyes family, both with leg injuries serious enough to require surgery. They faced months in casts. A GoFundMe was set up to help the family cover costs, with a goal of $100,000.Travis Kelce's foundation hit that target alone.Two $50,000 donations landed in the GoFundMe from Eighty-Seven and Running, singlehandedly matching the entire goal while over a thousand other donors were still contributing. The family released a statement: "On behalf of the Reyes Family, we are incredibly grateful for the love, support, and prayers during this difficult time. Our family, along with the other families impacted by this senseless act, are still healing physically and emotionally."Kelce himself posted on X shortly after the tragedy: "I am heartbroken over the tragedy that took place today. My heart is with all who came out to celebrate with us and have been affected. KC, you mean the world to me."That was it. No follow-up. No announcement of the donation. The money spoke for itself.Taylor Swift had separately donated $100,000 to the family of Lisa Lopez-Galvan, the local radio DJ who was killed. Together, the couple put $200,000 into the Kansas City community within days of the shooting. But Kelce's contribution carried a specific weight. He did not wait for a charity partner to organize it. He did not route it through a campaign. He identified the family that needed help and wrote the checks.What does Travis Kelce's $100,000 donation say about his character off the field?Athletes get credited for philanthropy all the time, often for donations announced louder than the impact they create. Travis Kelce's response to the parade shooting was the opposite of that. It was quiet, fast, and personal.This is someone who has contributed nearly $2 million to Operation Breakthrough over the years, helped build a hands-on learning center called the Ignition Lab that has reached 1,000 students since 2020, and won the NFL's Walter Payton Man of the Year Charity Challenge three times, a record no other player holds. The $100,000 for the Reyes family was not a headline strategy. It was a reflex.Patrick Mahomes and his wife Brittany visited the children in hospital. Kelce sent the money. Both mattered. But the check told you something specific: when Kelce sees a gap, he fills it. Quietly and without waiting to be asked.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: NFL News: Brittany Mahomes made a striking bridal statement when she married Patrick Mahomes in Hawaii in March 2022. Rather than choosing a traditional, unders.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes made a striking bridal statement when she married Patrick Mahomes in Hawaii in March 2022. Rather than choosing a traditional, understated gown, she walked down the aisle in a custom Versace creation that blended glamour, drama and modern bridal style. Designed with intricate crystal details and a figure-skimming silhouette, the dress quickly became one of the most memorable details of the couple’s Maui wedding.Brittany Mahomes’ Versace wedding dress featured a daring designFor her wedding to the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback, Brittany worked with celebrity stylist Mimi Cuttrell and the Versace team to create a gown made specifically for her. The result was a sleek, glamorous look that felt distinctly different from a classic princess-style wedding dress.The custom Versace wedding dress featured a corset-inspired bodice with strategic cutouts and sparkling crystal embellishments. Its structured design highlighted Brittany’s silhouette while keeping the overall look polished and luxurious.The back added another dramatic touch. Criss-cross straps gave the gown a modern finish, while a sweeping train extended behind her as she walked. A bustle helped manage the long train, making the elaborate dress more practical for the celebrations that followed the ceremony.Brittany completed the bridal look with a long tulle veil, creating a soft contrast against the structured gown. The combination gave her wedding outfit two distinct moods: bold and glamorous up close, yet classic when viewed as a complete bridal ensemble.Her makeup artist, Ash K Holm, also celebrated the moment on Instagram, calling her "the most beautiful bride" and writing, "It was an honor to be apart of your special day."Brittany’s wedding Instagram post also revealed the creative team behind the custom look, with tags for Cuttrell, Versace and Donatella Versace, the fashion house’s creative director.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ Hawaii wedding styleThe bride’s fashion choices extended beyond her own gown. Patrick Mahomes opted for a gray suit with a matching vest and added a playful luxury detail with bedazzled loafers.Their daughter, Sterling Skye, then one year old, joined the family celebration in a white dress featuring a bow at the back. Her outfit complemented Brittany’s bridal look without competing with it.The wedding marked a major milestone for the couple, who had been together for years before saying their vows. Brittany and Patrick first met at Whitehouse High School in Texas and attended prom together in 2013. They began dating as teenagers and later became engaged in September 2020.By the time they married in Maui, they had already welcomed their daughter in February 2021. Brittany had also celebrated the lead-up to the ceremony with a glamorous bachelorette party and a Queen of Hearts-themed bridal shower.Still, among all the memorable details from the celebrations, her custom Versace wedding dress remained the defining fashion moment. With its crystal-covered corset, dramatic train, striking back and flowing veil, the gown captured Brittany’s preference for making a statement while giving her Hawaii wedding a distinctly high-fashion finish.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Travis Kelce’s reported $54.7 million Chiefs contract isn’t really a 3-year deal
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce is staying with the Kansas City Chiefs for another season, but the headline number attached to his new contract tells only part of the st.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is staying with the Kansas City Chiefs for another season, but the headline number attached to his new contract tells only part of the story. While the deal was reported as a three-year, $54.7 million agreement, the practical value is much smaller. The structure gives Kansas City a way to manage its salary cap while keeping its longtime star under contract as he approaches the final stage of his NFL career.Travis Kelce’s Chiefs contract is essentially a one-year dealAccording to a league source cited by The Athletic, Kelce’s agreement is essentially a one-year, $12 million guaranteed deal. The Chiefs then added contract language that allows the financial charge to be distributed across three seasons.That distinction matters because NFL contracts can look very different on paper compared with how they work in practice. Kansas City used a provision in the collective bargaining agreement that permits certain salary figures to be prorated over the length of a contract.As a result, Kelce’s deal will reportedly count about $4.9 million against the Chiefs’ salary cap in 2026. That figure drops to roughly $3.55 million in each of the following two seasons.For Kansas City, the immediate benefit is clear. The team can keep Kelce while avoiding a much larger salary-cap hit this year. That extra room could prove useful as the Chiefs continue building a roster around quarterback Patrick Mahomes.The three-year label, however, should not be taken to mean Kelce is expected to play through 2028 under the current agreement.Why Travis Kelce’s reported $54.7 million value is misleadingThe eye-catching $54.7 million figure comes largely from a $40 million bonus written into the contract for 2028. Kelce would receive that money if he remains on the Chiefs’ roster on June 8, 2027.In practical terms, that scenario appears highly unlikely. Before that date arrives, Kelce could retire, be released or negotiate another contract with Kansas City. That makes the massive bonus more of a contractual mechanism than realistic earnings.The structure also marks a notable change in how the Chiefs have handled veteran contracts. Kansas City has generally avoided spreading cap charges into future seasons when it does not expect a player to remain on the roster. Doing so can create dead money later, meaning the team can carry a cap charge for a player who is no longer contributing on the field.Kelce represents an unusual case. He is one of the most accomplished tight ends in NFL history and has played a central role in the Chiefs’ recent success. With his career nearing its final chapter, Kansas City appears willing to accept some future financial complications in exchange for greater flexibility now.So, while the headline says three years and $54.7 million, the reality is much simpler. Kelce has secured another season in Kansas City, while the Chiefs have created a contract structure designed to protect their short-term salary-cap flexibility.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NFL News: BTS’ Chicago concerts may be over, but the group’s two-day stop at Soldier Field has left behind an unexpected keepsake. During the soundcheck for the.
articles.body: BTS’ Chicago concerts may be over, but the group’s two-day stop at Soldier Field has left behind an unexpected keepsake. During the soundcheck for their second concert on August 28, all seven BTS members reportedly bought customized NFL footballs in Chicago. Photos of the footballs have now drawn attention online, with each ball appearing to carry the member’s name alongside a special BTS world tour reference.BTS members receive customized NFL footballs during Chicago concertThe personalized footballs stood out as an unusual souvenir from BTS’ Chicago visit. Rather than picking up standard merchandise, the members got NFL-style footballs customized with their individual names.Images shared online show the red-and-white football design, with the words “BTS: WORLD TOUR” printed prominently on the white section. The balls also feature the dates “AUGUST 27 & 28, 2026,” matching the two dates of BTS’ Chicago concerts.The original post that brought attention to the footballs stated:“It seems all BTS members received a custom NFL football in Chicago, with their name and "BTS: WORLD TOUR (ARIRANG?) / August 27 & 28,2026" printed on it🏈”The footballs were bought during the soundcheck for the second Chicago concert on August 28, giving the items a direct connection to the group’s final day at the venue. The timing also makes the keepsakes particularly memorable, as the members were preparing for the second of their two performances when they picked them up.One of the photos shows a member holding one of the customized footballs inside the stadium. Another offers a closer look at the design, making the printed wording and concert dates easier to spot.Fans were quick to focus on the small details, including the individual names on the footballs and the Chicago-themed setting. A fan account highlighted the personalized nature of the gift while sharing its own reaction to the photos:“Hobi holding a customized "j-hope" NFL Football, must be from Chicago Bears? And everything else is of course curated for my man! The Black and Red theme of his shirt, scarf, the Chicago Bull cap, paired with his Chrome Hearts pants, looking so COOL and handsome as always 😍”While the images give fans a clear look at the footballs, the biggest appeal lies in their connection to BTS’ Chicago concerts. The dates printed on the balls turn what could have been a simple sports souvenir into a keepsake tied specifically to the group’s August 27 and 28 performances.Soldier Field: Chicago's historic stadiumSoldier Field is one of Chicago’s best-known sporting venues, with a history stretching back more than a century. The multi-purpose stadium opened in 1924 and has hosted football, soccer, concerts and major international sporting events.The venue has been the home of the Chicago Bears of the NFL since 1971. It also became the home of Chicago Fire FC in 2020. With a football capacity of 62,500, Soldier Field is the second-smallest stadium in the NFL.Its history extends far beyond professional football. Soldier Field has hosted matches during the 1994 FIFA World Cup and the 1999 FIFA Women’s World Cup, along with multiple CONCACAF Gold Cup championships. It also staged the inaugural World Games of the Special Olympics in 1968 and hosted the event again in 1970.The stadium underwent a major interior reconstruction in 2002 and 2003, bringing modern facilities to the historic venue. Despite those changes, Soldier Field remains a landmark part of Chicago’s sporting and cultural landscape.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: NFL News: Brittany Mahomes called her latest Kansas City Chiefs game-day outing “Straight chaos 😎❤️.” Her outfit looked far more coordinated than the caption s.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes called her latest Kansas City Chiefs game-day outing “Straight chaos 😎❤️.” Her outfit looked far more coordinated than the caption suggested.Mahomes attended Friday’s preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium with members of her family. Patrick Mahomes did not play as Kansas City and Seattle finished in a 9-9 tie, but Brittany still arrived in a game-day look built around one clear theme: blue.What did Brittany Mahomes wear to Patrick Mahomes’ Chiefs preseason game?Brittany paired blue denim micro shorts with a cropped jacket in a similar wash. She wore a white T-shirt underneath and finished the outfit with blue Adidas sneakers.The shoes made the coordination obvious. Instead of switching to a neutral sneaker, Brittany carried the same color family from the denim into her footwear. She also wore rose-colored sunglasses and kept her blonde hair down, straight and side-parted.Brittany shared footage from the outing on Instagram after attending the Aug. 28 game. Us Weekly reported that she brought Sterling and Bronze to Arrowhead, while Golden did not appear to attend.Sterling, 5, wore a gray “Chiefs Kingdom” dress with a red bow in her hair. Bronze, 3, wore a red polo with Chiefs branding.The family appearance came as Kansas City completed another preseason game ahead of the 2026 regular season. Patrick remained on the sideline Friday rather than taking snaps against Seattle.The actual game offered little separation between the teams. Kansas City and Seattle traded field goals before finishing tied at nine. Seahawks kicker Jason Myers had a chance to break the tie at the end, but he missed a 52-yard field goal as time expired.For Brittany, the appearance also continued a pattern that has become familiar during Patrick’s NFL career. She regularly attends Chiefs games and has used game days for Chiefs-themed outfits, family appearances and posts from Arrowhead.This time, the blue-on-blue combination moved away from Kansas City’s usual red-heavy color palette. The Chiefs branding came through more directly in Sterling and Bronze’s clothes.What has Brittany Mahomes said about supporting Patrick Mahomes through NFL seasons?The photos may focus on clothes and family, but Brittany has also spoken openly about what life around an NFL season requires.In a February interview with Sports Illustrated, the Kansas City Current co-owner discussed the work that can come with being the partner of an NFL player.“I think being the significant other to an NFL player is an incredibly hard role, and we take on a lot of important stuff behind the scenes that people don’t get to see,” Brittany said. “We also get to enjoy life and do things that we love, too.”Patrick has publicly made the same point from his side of their marriage.During a 2024 appearance on the “Impaulsive” podcast, the three-time Super Bowl champion credited Brittany with handling much of their life away from football.“I think people don’t even realize how much she does,” Patrick said. “I mean, taking care of the day-to-day stuff and make it where I can focus on football and focus on my craft and everything like that. [She’s] a Hall of Fame mom and a Hall of Fame wife, [which] makes it a lot easier.”Patrick and Brittany began dating while they were in high school and married in 2022. They now have three children.Friday gave Brittany another chance to bring that family side of the Mahomes household to Arrowhead. Patrick never entered the game, the Chiefs never found the end zone, and nobody left with a preseason win.Brittany still found a way to make blue Adidas sneakers and a double-denim set part of the Chiefs conversation before the regular season begins.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla accidentally picks a fight with his own fanbase on day one
articles.summary: NFL News: Vinod Khosla just bought the Seattle Seahawks for a record $9.6 billion, and during his very first press conference as an owner, he casually dropped a.
articles.body: Vinod Khosla just bought the Seattle Seahawks for a record $9.6 billion, and during his very first press conference as an owner, he casually dropped a bomb that became a PR nightmare. He admitted that he’s been a lifelong Pittsburgh Steelers fan, and he still watches every one of their games. Reporters and fans reacted immediately, they all roasted him, saying that this might be the worst possible thing to say on day one. Now Khosla is firing back at the media, accusing them of blowing up a "molehill" for clicks. Here's exactly what he said, what the backlash looked like, and what he's saying now to defend himself.What Vinod Khosla actually said at the press conferenceKhosla explained his Steelers loyalty goes back decades. He said he came to the US in 1976, right when Pittsburgh was dominating the NFL, and that's what hooked him on football. "I was originally and still am a big Steelers fan," he told reporters, adding, "little-known fact, but I still watch all the Steelers games, too."The timing made it awkward. The Seahawks' only Super Bowl loss came against the Steelers back in 2006, and the result is still bitterly remembered in Seattle. Barstool Sports posted the clip asking what not to do at your opening press conference as the new owner, and pointed out he'd just admitted the exact thing.Vinod Khosla gave the media a slapback for making it a storyKhosla isn't shying away from it. He hit back on X, calling the coverage a media strategy to fill "column inches" and "video minutes," and insisted his old fandom changes nothing about how he'll run the team. "I still watch their games doesn't mean I won't unconditionally ALWAYS as owner, want [the Seahawks] to win," he wrote, adding he wants Seattle to have "every edge up, EVERY TIME over every other team." He even signed off sarcastically, thanking reporters for the extra pageviews.There's a wrinkle worth noting too: Khosla previously held a small stake in the San Francisco 49ers, which NFL rules now require him to sell as part of taking over Seattle. His wife Neeru Khosla is set to be the franchise's controlling owner, with son Neal and daughter Nina also part of the family group fronting the purchase.Honestly, this isn't the scandal media wants it to be, but it's not nothing either. Nobody's questioning whether Khosla will run the Seahawks to win, he just paid $9.6 billion for the privilege, that's motivation enough.The real issue is that he didn't need to say any of it. A billionaire buying his first NFL team gets exactly one shot at a first impression, and he chose to spend it reminiscing about a rival franchise that broke Seattle's heart in 2006. That's not media manufacturing outrage, that's just bad instincts for the room. Calling reporters out for covering your own unprompted quote doesn't fix that either; it just makes day one stretch into day three.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Daejon Love case explained: How a fake 49ers player allegedly fooled 26 women and pulled off a $1,300,000 scam
articles.summary: NFL News: Picture this: a match on a dating app with a guy who says he plays wide receiver for the San Francisco 49ers. He shows up to the first date in a jerse.
articles.body: Picture this: a match on a dating app with a guy who says he plays wide receiver for the San Francisco 49ers. He shows up to the first date in a jersey, a helmet in the back seat of his car, like he just walked off practice. He talks about a future together, about investments that'll make you both rich. You believe him, and why wouldn't you? He even showed you the Google search proving it. Then one day the calls stop, the messages stop, and you're left wondering where your money went.Daejon Love: the man who faked being a 49ers player, bought a $1,160 helmet, and scammed 26 women out of $1.3 millionThat's the story 26 women say they lived through with Daejon Labrayae Love, 35, except he never played a single down for the 49ers. On August 24, the FBI arrested Love and his 18-year-old accomplice Taylor Jamie Chan at Boise Airport, where he'd reportedly gone to meet new victims.Federal prosecutors say the pair ran a romance-and-investment scam across California, Oregon, Washington, and Idaho for over four years, taking $1.3 million, and the FBI believes many more victims haven't come forward yet.Here's everything that's surfaced since, including the one detail that's making the internet lose it.Love met most victims on dating apps like Tinder, Bumble, Hinge, and Facebook Dating and then built entire fake lives around them. He posed as a 49ers player under aliases including Jon Love, Jordan Love, and Avril Lyto Love, and separately claimed to be a wealthy real estate investor. Chan played the "financial adviser," backing up his fake investment pitches so victims believed their money was actually growing somewhere.Court documents describe just how far Love went to sell it. He allegedly spent over $1,160 on a custom replica helmet from a football gear vendor, filmed himself "signing" a fake 49ers contract while dripping in jewelry, and even showed up to a first date in a jersey with a helmet sitting in his car.When victims got suspicious, prosecutors say he'd send them screenshots of Google's AI Overview falsely listing him as an NFL player, and if they pushed back, his line was reportedly, "That's Google, that's not me." Once someone ran out of money or asked too many questions, he cut them off and kept whatever they'd sent.The internet's reaction has been brutalOnce the case went public, former NFL linebacker Su'a Cravens couldn't hold back, joking that victims should've just tried to FaceTime him on game day. Sports accounts piled on with a running joke that the 49ers' offseason had somehow gotten messier than the season itself between a Brandon Aiyuk contract standoff, owner Jed York's arrest, Kyle Shanahan's car accident, and now a guy who invented an entire fake roster spot.Both Love and Chan are in federal custody in Boise facing wire fraud and conspiracy charges, with an initial court appearance already held. Nothing has been proven in court yet, and both are presumed innocent, but if even a fraction of what prosecutors allege is true, this might be the most elaborate catfish the NFL world has ever indirectly been dragged into.Would a real player really need a Google search to prove it? The Jacksonville Jaguars have acquired former University of Texas star Quinn Ewers as a depth option behind Trevor Lawrence.

The Jaguars acquired Ewers from the Miami Dolphins in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo first reported the trade.

Here's a look at both team's projected quarterback depth charts following the trade.

The Miami Herald 's Barry Jackson reported Ewers had support within the Dolphins coaching staff "but the front office was displeased by his training camp performance."

"There was sentiment in front office for a different No. 2," Jackson reported.

Ewers, selected in the seventh round of the 2025 draft, made four appearances and three starts for the Dolphins in his rookie season.

He saw most of his action last season when starting the Dolphins' final three games, completing 66.7 percent of his passes for 569 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions over that span.

Ewers made just one appearance for the Dolphins this preseason in an Aug. 14 matchup against the Washington Commanders in which he went 1-for-8 and later said he was playing through a pulled groin muscle.

That injury sidelined Ewers for the Dolphins' final two preseason games. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley had yet to officially name a backup quarterback at the time of the Ewers trade.

The Dolphins will now be left with two inexperienced backup options barring another trade. Cam Miller spent last season with the Las Vegas Raiders practice squad, while Mark Gronowski is a 2026 undrafted free agent out of Iowa.

The Jaguars may need to move a signal caller out of their crowded room before the roster cutdown deadline hits Sunday at 6 p.m. ET.

With Nick Mullens set to back up Lawrence, the Jaguars could choose between Ewers, Carter Bradley and Joey Aguilar as a third-string option.

Bradley spent two seasons with the Raiders and San Francisco 49ers practice squads before he was signed to the Jaguars' practice squad last season. Aguilar signed with the Jaguars earlier this offseason as an undrafted free agent out of Tennessee.

articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens traded offensive tackle Diego Pounds to the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens traded offensive tackle Diego Pounds to the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo .

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Ravens' compensation in the trade is contingent on the picks that Kansas City has available at the end of the 2026 season, resulting in either a Day 3 2027 pick or a Day 3 2028 pick heading to Baltimore.

Pounds, an undrafted rookie, will undergo a change of scenery before teams are required to trim their rosters to 53 players on Sunday.

He spent four years in college with North Carolina and Ole Miss before joining the Ravens after the 2026 draft.

The 23-year-old was effective throughout the start of the preseason for Baltimore prior to the trade.

Pounds' 90.9 overall grade from Pro Football Focus through two preseason weeks represented the highest mark of any offensive lineman, as he didn't allow a sack, hurry or quarterback hit in 15 pass-blocking snaps.

Still, he might not have done enough to earn a spot on Baltimore's 53-man roster and was traded instead of potentially getting cut.

Meanwhile, Kansas City has continued to make offensive line additions as Week 1 draws closer. The team previously acquired lineman Josh Ezeudu in a trade with the New York Giants on Wednesday.

It's worth noting that Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons is currently dealing with a back injury , although head coach Andy Reid confirmed that he was optimistic about Simmons' return to practice on Friday.

"Yes," Reid said, per Pete Sweeney of the Kansas City Star . "It's going to take a little bit of time here. He's a hard worker when it comes to these types of things. It's just a matter of eliminating some of the pain that he has — and strength, making sure he has enough strength there."

As Simmons continues to recover, the Chiefs bolstered their depth behind him by adding Pounds.

articles.title: Grade the trade: Cowboys take a chance on former Steelers first-round pick, OT Broderick Jones
articles.summary: The Cowboys got some insurance behind their offensive tackles.
articles.body:
There was excitement for the Pittsburgh Steelers when they drafted Georgia offensive tackle Broderick Jones with the 14th overall NFL Draft pick in 2023. They even traded up to take him.

The excitement ran out Saturday when the Steelers reportedly traded Jones to the Dallas Cowboys . The Cowboys sent a third- and sixth-round pick to the Steelers for Jones and a fourth-round pick, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

Jones had dealt with a neck injury and had not been the player the Steelers thought they were getting. He had struggled to become a reliable tackle. He was in the mix to start for the Steelers this season but when Max Iheanachor, this year's first-round pick by Pittsburgh, made his preseason debut Thursday then Jones became expendable.

For the Cowboys, it's one of the chances they often take on players who were graded highly coming out of college but didn't work out with their first team.

The Cowboys have a solid line but that's mostly on the interior. Left tackle Tyler Guyton has not played up to his first-round billing through his two seasons, Terence Steele is a serviceable right tackle and there isn't much proven depth behind them.

Jones can be a backup at either tackle position. He has not been great in the NFL yet but he is just 25 years old and is an upgrade over what Dallas had at backup swing tackle. Jones has a big medical red flag after spinal fusion surgery last year, but the Cowboys appear comfortable with that risk.

Trading back from the third to fourth round and sending a sixth-round pick isn't cheap for a tackle with a rough health history and also struggles on the field. But team owner Jerry Jones likes reclamation projects, and Broderick Jones is an insurance policy at both tackle positions, which profile as the Cowboys' weakest two positions on offense.

Steelers move on after pick didn't work out

It's hard to move on quickly from a pick in the first half of the first round, but the writing was on the wall when the Steelers took Iheanachor in the first round this season.

Jones' spinal fusion surgery last year put his future in doubt, though he came back to play this preseason. Instead of holding onto Jones to be a backup at either right or left tackle, the Steelers decided they had seen enough from Jones and recouped some draft value for him.

It was a good return for the Steelers for a player who likely wasn't going to start and is in the final year of his rookie deal after his fifth-year options was declined. It stings to admit a big mistake on a valuable pick, but the Steelers did fine in the trade.

articles.body: Travis Kelce's growing business empire is no longer limited to the familiar world of celebrity endorsements. The Kansas City Chiefs star has steadily moved into ownership, investment and sports-related ventures, creating a portfolio that stretches from beer and sleep products to professional sports and college athletics. His latest moves suggest Kelce is thinking well beyond his NFL career and building a business identity that can stand on its own.Travis Kelce expands his business empire beyond endorsementsKelce's business portfolio has grown because he has increasingly chosen opportunities where he can play a bigger role than simply appearing in an advertisement. One of the clearest examples is his involvement with Garage Beer, the Ohio-based beer company he co-owns with his brother, Jason Kelce.The brand has become a notable part of Kelce's business profile, particularly as it expands its reach. His connection to the company also fits naturally with the image he has built around his Ohio roots and his wider appeal outside football.His interests also extend into the wellness space. Kelce became an investor and brand ambassador for Sleep Number, linking his personal experience as a professional athlete with a product built around sleep and recovery. That relationship gives him a direct connection to a category that matters to athletes while also reaching a much broader consumer audience.Kelce has also entered the restaurant business through 1587 Prime, a steakhouse in Kansas City created with Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes. The venture adds hospitality to a portfolio that already spans consumer brands, media and sports.Travis Kelce moves into college sports and MLB ownershipKelce's newest business interests show an even broader ambition. Through TEKTA, a venture backed by Publicis, he is stepping into the rapidly changing world of college athlete marketing and NIL.Rather than simply benefiting from his own marketability, Kelce is positioning himself to help brands work with college athletes. His experience as a major sports personality gives the venture a useful perspective on how athletes can build commercial value while connecting with audiences.The move comes alongside another significant expansion into professional sports ownership. Kelce has joined the ownership group of the Cleveland Guardians, giving him a stake in a Major League Baseball franchise.That investment carries an obvious personal connection. Kelce was raised in the Cleveland area before becoming one of the NFL's biggest stars. Becoming part of the Guardians ownership group therefore brings his business interests back to the city where his sporting journey began.Taken together, these ventures reveal a clear pattern. articles.body: Tom Brady built his life around football for more than two decades. Retirement has changed his role, but it has not slowed his pace. The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback remains deeply involved in football, business and his work with the Las Vegas Raiders. At the same time, Brady says his children have become a bigger priority as he looks back on the final chapter of his playing career.Tom Brady opens up about family life after NFL retirementBrady's life away from the NFL still leaves little room for downtime. Speaking to PEOPLE, the seven-time Super Bowl champion admitted that his packed schedule has made personal time difficult, even as he continues to enjoy the work in front of him.“I don't have much time for a personal life or much time for myself, but I love working and I love my kids,” Brady told PEOPLE.His comments offer a glimpse into the balance he is trying to maintain years after his 2022 divorce from Gisele Bündchen. The end of their marriage led to intense public speculation about Brady's decision to continue playing, but both have indicated that the situation was more complicated than one explanation.Brady has also reflected on the point when he knew it was time to leave football behind. After 23 NFL seasons, he felt he had reached a stage where spending more time with his children mattered more than extending his playing career.“I had 23 years of [football] so I didn’t think I was missing anything, retiring,” Brady said. “I felt like I always had a goal... 45."I was 45 years old, I wanted to spend time with my kids, I felt like, okay, now it’s time for me to be at all my kids’ games. They’ve been to enough of their dad’s games.”The decision came after a difficult final season. Brady finished his career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but the circumstances surrounding that period made it a particularly challenging year.“I felt like I owed to my teammates and coaches to give them everything I had,” Brady said. “I wish it could have been a little bit better at the end. articles.title: Career turning point: "Anytime you lose a Super Bowl, it's the worst thing in the world...it will stick with you the rest of your career"- Patrick Mahomes reveals what Chiefs' loss means for his future
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes had spent years making the Super Bowl feel almost routine. Then came a night in New Orleans that exposed the other side of that succes.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes had spent years making the Super Bowl feel almost routine. Then came a night in New Orleans that exposed the other side of that success. After the Kansas City Chiefs were beaten 40-22 by the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl LIX, Mahomes stood in front of reporters and spoke about a pain he knew would not disappear quickly. His message was clear: the defeat would become part of what drives him.Patrick Mahomes spoke after Chiefs' Super Bowl LIX lossMahomes made the remarks during his postgame press conference at Caesars Superdome on February 9, 2025. The setting could hardly have been more difficult for the Chiefs quarterback.Kansas City had arrived with a chance to make NFL history. A victory would have made the Chiefs the first team to win three straight Super Bowls. Instead, Philadelphia controlled the game and ended Kansas City's bid for a historic three-peat.Mahomes did not try to hide from his role in the collapse.When asked about the Eagles' defense, he gave them credit for the way they played from start to finish. He also accepted responsibility for his own mistakes, particularly the turnovers that helped Philadelphia seize control.“I can’t turn the ball over early in the game when it’s not going our way,” Mahomes said after the loss, acknowledging that he needed to learn from what happened and improve the next time he got the opportunity.That accountability became one of the strongest themes of his postgame comments.The quarterback had thrown three touchdown passes, but his two interceptions and a lost fumble came at damaging moments. Philadelphia turned those mistakes into points, while its defense repeatedly pressured Kansas City's offense.The result was unlike the close Super Bowl finishes that had defined much of Mahomes' career.Patrick Mahomes compared Eagles defeat with Super Bowl LV lossThe question that produced his memorable quote asked Mahomes to compare the Eagles loss with Kansas City's defeat against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers four years earlier.His answer captured just how deeply Super Bowl defeats can affect a player who has experienced the highest level of success."Anytime you lose a Super Bowl, it's the worst thing in the world... it will stick with you the rest of your career"Mahomes had good reason to make that comparison. Super Bowl LV had ended with Tampa Bay beating Kansas City 31-9, another painful defeat on the biggest stage.The two losses were different in their details, but they shared one brutal feature. Both left Mahomes and the Chiefs far short of the standard they had set.The quarterback then explained that the defeats could serve a purpose. Rather than allowing the losses to define him, he viewed them as reminders of what it takes to finish the job when another championship opportunity arrives.Mahomes has often spoken about the value of learning from difficult moments. This time, however, the lesson came after one of the most painful nights of his professional career.Why the Super Bowl loss mattered so much to Patrick MahomesThe defeat carried more weight because of what Kansas City had already accomplished.The Chiefs had become one of the NFL's defining teams under Mahomes and Andy Reid. They had won three Super Bowls in five seasons and reached the championship game five times in six years.That level of success changes expectations. A season that ends without a championship can feel like failure when a team has become accustomed to playing in February.Mahomes understood that better than most.He had already experienced the emotional difference between winning and losing at the highest level. After the Eagles defeat, he acknowledged that the pain of the losses could remain with him longer than the joy of some victories.That sentiment was echoed by Chiefs coach Andy Reid, who said the loss would hurt because of how much work players and coaches invest in reaching the Super Bowl.The defeat also ended a remarkable run of dominance. Kansas City had entered the game seeking a third consecutive championship, a feat no NFL team had accomplished.Instead, the Eagles' defense dismantled the Chiefs' offense and forced Mahomes into one of the toughest games of his career.Patrick Mahomes vowed to use the defeat as fuelWhat made Mahomes' comments notable was not simply the disappointment. It was what he intended to do with it.The quarterback did not describe the loss as something he wanted to forget. He viewed it as a permanent reminder.His message was especially striking because he had already experienced three Super Bowl victories before turning 30. That success has made his standard unusually high, but it has also given him a clear understanding of how rare these opportunities are.Mahomes knows a team cannot assume it will return to the Super Bowl every year. Injuries, competition and small mistakes can end a championship run in an instant.That is why the Eagles loss could become an important chapter in his career.The Chiefs still had a championship-caliber quarterback, a respected coaching staff and a roster capable of competing at the highest level. But the defeat exposed areas that needed attention. Mahomes' turnovers were among them, and he made no attempt to shift blame elsewhere.The response also showed the mindset that has helped define his career. He was disappointed, but he was already looking toward the next opportunity.For Mahomes, the lasting impact of Super Bowl LIX may not be the score or the frustration of watching Philadelphia celebrate. It may be the memory of how the game felt and the lessons he takes from it.That is what gives his words lasting significance.Super Bowl losses can become scars. For Mahomes, they can also become fuel. His challenge now is to make sure the memory of the Eagles' dominant victory pushes him toward a stronger version of himself when Kansas City gets another chance to play for the Lombardi Trophy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Jaguars add another option behind Trevor Lawrence

Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) greets Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) after the game of an NFL football AFC Wild Card playoff matchup, Sunday, Jan. 11, 2026, in Jacksonville, Fla. The Bills defeated the Jaguars 27-24. [Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union]

Ewers, 23, was selected by Miami in the seventh round of the 2025 NFL Draft after a standout college career at Texas. He appeared in four games for the Dolphins as a rookie, making three starts after Miami benched Tua Tagovailoa late in the season.

articles.title: NFL waiver wire explained: Which Detroit Lions are impacted
articles.summary: What is the NFL waiver wire system and which current Detroit Lions players are subject to the process?
articles.body:
The NFL and the Detroit Lions will close out their preseason on Saturday, and by 6 p.m. ET Sunday, teams must reduce their rosters to 53 players. For the Lions, that will mean removing 38 players from their 91-man offseason roster, a daunting task that will need to be accomplished in roughly 24 hours after they finish out the preseason.

This look at the waiver wire process and how it impacts the Lions roster was sponsored by FanDuel Sportsbook , which currently has the Lions listed at +1700 to win this year's Super Bowl, +850 to win the NFC Championship, and +155 to win the NFC North as the current favorites.

As Jeremy Reisman explained in a roster cuts rules article , when a player is cut from the roster, they'll fall into two categories: "waived" or "released." The category a player falls into depends on how many "credited" seasons in the NFL they have. A player earns a credited season if they spent at least three games in a season on the active roster, or the season on IR, or PUP .

A player with four or more credited seasons is designated as "released," meaning they immediately become a free agent. A player with fewer than four credited seasons is "waived" and therefore subject to the NFL's waiver system, where another NFL team can claim them and keep their contract intact.

Which Lions are eligible for the waiver wire?

This offseason, the Lions got younger across the roster, and as a result, 57 of their 91 players have fewer than four credited seasons. Here's a list of those players:

Here's an at-a-glance look at the Lions' current depth chart, with the players eligible for the waiver wire colored by position and the vested veterans without color:

From cutdowns through the first three weeks of the regular season, the waiver wire priority is determined by last year's NFL Draft order, with teams in their original slots. That means the Lions will have 17th priority in the waiver wire process . Therefore, if they put in a claim for a "waived" player and the 16 teams ahead of them in the order do not put in a claim, Detroit will be awarded that player.

Once a player is waived from any team, they become eligible for the waiver wire process, which begins immediately following cutdowns (Sunday at 6 p.m. ET) and ends on Monday at 1 p.m. ET. Once the deadline passes, the NFL will sort through the claims and award players based on waiver wire priority, with the highest priority getting first dibs.

Once a waived player is claimed by a team, that player is immediately placed on the team's 53-man roster, and the team has until the end of the business day (typically only a few hours) to make a corresponding roster move. If the player cut to make room is eligible for the waiver wire, the process begins for them; they become eligible at 4 p.m. ET that day, and their waiver wire window closes the next day around noon.

What happens if a player is not claimed?

If a player is not claimed off waivers, they immediately become an unrestricted free agent and are eligible to sign with any team or to their practice squad.

When do teams start building their practice squad?

Once the initial waiver wire window expires (Monday at 1 p.m. ET), teams may begin building their 16-player practice squad—be on the lookout for our Practice Squad Tracker, which will publish on Sunday.

The number was going to 12 players for 2 years, and then was going to be increased to 14 players in 2022. That all changed when the uncertainty of COVID-19 hit, and the league increased practice squads to 16 players, which will once again be the limit in 2025.

Teams participating in the International Player Pathway(IPP) program can have 91-man rosters during the offseason. They can also have a 17th practice squad member for the season, but if signed to the practice squad, that player can't be signed to the regular season roster; however, starting in 2024 he can be elevated for up to three games. If the player is kept on the 53-man roster, he is subject to waiver rules.

The Washington Commanders currently have DE T.J. Maguranyanga on the roster, and he is eligible to be signed to their practice squad as the 17th member if he is waived and clears waivers. He is unlikely to be part of the 53-man roster.

Practice squad players moving up to the main roster

Like the last three seasons, teams have more flexibility with using practice squad players on game day. PS players can be activated on game day before the team announces their inactives(90 minutes before game time). Teams are allowed to elevate players from their practice squad to the game day roster without having to cut a member of the 53-man team. Accordingly, clubs can increase from the standard 53 to 55 players while game day active squads expand from a previous 46 to 47 players (or 48 if a team carries eight offensive linemen). Any practice squad player can be elevated and automatically reverts back to the practice squad after a game.

Each practice squad player is now able to be elevated up to three times per season. To be activated a fourth time requires the player to be signed to the regular roster. During the playoffs, practice squad players have unlimited elevations. This makes it easier for teams to have players they know and trust on game day, and also not have to subject them to waivers when they are signed to the main roster and cut to get back to the practice squad as was true in the past.

Another change is the eligibility requirements for veteran players. Previously teams could have up to 4 players who had two years of NFL experience. Now teams can have 6 veterans with no limit on the amount of accrued seasons they have in the league. A player must have been on full-play status for at least six regular-season games in a given season to gain an accrued season. This includes being on the active/inactive list, injured reserve or reserve PUP.

Practice squad players make $13,750 per week or $247,500 for 18 weeks. Veteran players with over two years of experience make a minimum of $18,350 per week or $330,300 for 18 weeks, and a maximum of $22,8590 per week or $411,300 for 18 weeks.

Teams must complete their roster cuts by Sunday August 30th at 6 p.m. ET, meaning that almost 1,200 players will be released or placed on an injury list.

Teams have until Monday at noon to claim unvested players that have been waived.

Vested veterans (players with a minimum of 4 accrued seasons) become free agents immediately and are able to sign with any team.

Starting at 12:00 p.m. ET on August 31st, teams can begin signing players to their practice squads.

Practice squad players practice with the team. They do not play in games, unless they are elevated (see above)

Practice squad players are paid per week and can be released at any point during the season.

Practice squad players are free to sign with other NFL teams, but they have to be signed to the 53-man active roster of the acquiring team. A practice squad player cannot be signed to another practice squad unless he is first released or waived.

A practice squad player cannot sign with his team's upcoming opponent unless he does so six days before the upcoming game, or 10 days if his team is currently on a bye week.

If a practice squad player is signed to the active roster, he will receive a minimum of three weekly paychecks, even if he is released before spending three weeks with the new team.

In order to be signed to a practice squad after being released, a player who is not a vested veteran must first clear waivers, and is subject to waiver claims by other teams.

The Washington Commanders had the No. 7 overall pick in this year's draft, which means they have six teams in front of them that could potentially claim a player Washington wants. There should be plenty of players available, and Washington will be on the look out for some offensive line help next week.

The waiver order goes by original draft order not counting trades.

Teams maintain their places on the waiver priority list through Week 3 of the regular season.

After Week 3 the waiver priority order is determined by reverse order of wins.

Teams don't lose their spot on the priority list like in fantasy football.

Teams can put in as many waiver claims as they want, and will be awarded the player(s) if they are the highest-ranked claiming team. Any player added through waivers will need a corresponding roster move to make room for him on the roster.

Vested veterans(on an NFL roster for at least 6 games per season, for at least 4 seasons) aren't subject to waivers until after the trade deadline, which will be after Week 9 this season.

Players who are waived/injured, and not claimed on waivers, return to their team and are placed on injured reserve unless an injury settlement is made.

articles.title: As Colts weigh backup QB decision, Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard keep cheering each other on
articles.summary: 'I'm rooting for Riley': On the relationship between Riley Leonard and Anthony Richardson in battle for Colts backup quarterback job
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS – In the highest moment of his second NFL preseason, Colts quarterback Riley Leonard was looking for his mentor.

But when he turned around in the end zone at the edge of a celebratory scrum to find starting quarterback Daniel Jones , Leonard almost ran into his part-time rival and full-time teammate.

Anthony Richardson Sr. was there for one person: Riley.

As nearly the entire Colts bench poured onto the field in the moments immediately following DJ Giddens ' 6-yard scamper into the end zone for the team's lone touchdown in more than two weeks, Richardson recognized that there was more than one person to celebrate. After all, Giddens scored – or was able to score, really – because Leonard had connected on a couple key strikes in what looked, for a moment, like the second-year quarterback's only plays of the game.

See photos from the Indianapolis Colts against the Detroit Lions

Richardson has been in his share of quarterback battles – last year for the starting position, this summer to be the backup – and the former fourth-overall pick knew just how big it was that Leonard had marched the Colts down the field on a scoring drive when his number was called.

When either has been on the field this preseason, their end-goal has been to do what it takes to win the job. But when the ball isn't in the air, they're each other's biggest fan.

"Coach told us that we've got to bring the juice, be excited when we make plays, but I was more excited for Riley on his drive and making it happen, because it feels good as a quarterback, mobbing the ball and eventually putting up points," Richardson told reporters after the game of the second quarter celebratory moment. "I was more excited for (Leonard) than DJ – but don't tell DJ I said that!"

Colts head coach Shane Steichen told reporters last week that he has no timeline on when to announce Jones' backup ahead of Indianapolis' Week 1 game against the Ravens on Sept. 13, and Steichen wouldn't commit to that decision being set in stone once it comes down.

"We'll see. I mean, it's a big week for both those guys this week – to go out and practice is going to be important, and those game reps are going to be important as well," Steichen said on Tuesday.

Said more pointedly Saturday afternoon by principal team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon during an interview in the local broadcast booth: "We were talking about the 'Find a way' consistency, it's something you need to see, and you get to your backup quarterbacks. We have two young guys with talent and potential, but we need to see more consistency.

"I think we saw it today with Anthony; I think Riley's got a lot of potential. He's a hard worker, he's got a great attitude, but it takes a little while. It takes a while for them to develop their skills."

Leonard, drafted in the sixth round in 2025 as a project who had zero expectation to play as a rookie, was thrust into the fold as Indianapolis' quarterback picture went from crystal-clear to battered to downright worrisome. Unexpectedly, the 23-year-old made his meaningful NFL debut in Jacksonville in the moments immediately after Jones tore his right Achilles tendon – a disaster that sent a team already in a tailspin into a freefall. Though he managed the offense as best he could, Indianapolis would lose that game and board the plane ride home worrying their rookie third-string QB had a knee injury. With Richardson sidelined due to a fractured orbital bone suffered in a freak pre-game accident two months prior, Steichen rang Philip Rivers on the couch.

After nearly five years of retirement, Rivers returned to the game seven days later. In the season-finale, when Leonard was given the reins to make his first-career start, the Colts having already been eliminated from the playoffs, the rookie played freely – not without blemishes, but without largely any pressure.

Flash-forward to this summer, and the weight of the moment is seemingly where he's struggled the most. Even in otherwise innocuous practice reps with the second and third teams, Leonard has struggled holding onto the ball too long.

Meanwhile, Richardson scrambles with reckless abandon, slinging it wherever he so chooses. At times, the strikes are living proof that the arm of a fourth-overall pick from three years ago still exists, but there continue to be moments where you can't help but shake or scratch your head and wonder…

Consistency, simply put, has not defined this quarterback battle. Five quarters of playing time has left Richardson 21-of-33 for 249 yards passing, zero touchdowns through the air (one on the ground) and a fumble and an interception. Leonard's figures, though marginally worse – 20-for-42, 199 yards passing, zero touchdowns and two picks – don't make much material difference.

Though both have started NFL game(s), neither is proven as a solution if Jones – the quarterback who's only ever played an entire season once in a seven-year career – goes down.

And neither may see the field again beyond Saturday, which was why, they both said, it was important to bask in the little joys when they came – together.

"I think whenever you enter a QB competition, you've just got to keep reminding yourself, 'My best is good enough to win, and Anthony's best is good enough to win.' You never want to win a competition because maybe you both played bad, but you just didn't play as bad," Leonard said post-game Saturday. "Me and him are on the same page. 'Man, I'm rooting for you,' and I know he's rooting for me.

"(It's about) who can reach their full potential? Who can play to their full potential? He's someone I really respect and love. If there's one guy I wake up in the morning and go to the facility and I'm excited to see every day and joke around with, it's Anthony. It's been a really healthy competition, so I guess we'll find out where we stand."

Unfortunately for Leonard, there was more left in his story Saturday after the touchdown drive. His teammates would force and recover a fumble on the ensuing kickoff. After an 8-minute, 4-second drive from the Lions to start the second quarter gave Leonard and the Colts less than seven minutes, the Indianapolis offense would unexpectedly get the ball a second time – this drive starting just outside the red zone, offering a prime opportunity for more highlight-reel moments to try and shrink whatever gap may exist between he and Richardson.

"I thought the first drive went really well, but unfortunately, I got two drives," said Leonard postgame, succinctly summarizing the chaos that would ensue. A deep incompletion to Deion Burks was followed by what can only be described as a bounce pass in the flat to Anthony Gould. And then on third-down, Leonard stared down a free blitzer off the edge and chucked up a prayer to Gould down the left sideline.

Not too dissimilar to an ill-placed heave two weeks ago against New England, the ball was easily picked off, ending Leonard's day and his second preseason.

In reflection, it wasn't the throw itself that irked Leonard so much as his inability pre-snap to get his teammates in place to give himself more time to throw. The pass was where he wanted the ball to go – more importantly, he said, where it should have gone.

"I felt comfortable out there. I felt confident – even on the interception. It's like, alright, you know, it is what it is, but I felt good. I felt like I was hitting it pretty well," he said. "Every week has been a lot better for me, mentally. I don't know the stats or anything and whether it proves that or not, but mentally, each week, I truly felt better out there.

"I felt very prepared coming into this game."

Richardson, for whatever it may be worth, felt he played Saturday with confidence, too. Both players enter the final days of preparation for a season where neither knows what role they'll play or if they'll actually play at all.

Maybe but one thing is for certain: They'll be rooting for each other.

"I just wanna do my best, put my best foot forward, and God will take care of the rest," Richardson said. "I'm rooting for everyone to win. I want everyone to win. I want everyone to reach their goals and dreams and aspirations that everybody has wanted since they were little kids.

"I'm rooting for Riley, and I'm just trying to do my part and put my best foot forward and leave the rest up to God."

articles.title: San Francisco 49ers Part Ways With Veteran QB & Former UFL MVP
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers have released 1 veteran backup quarterback and former UFL MVP. The post San Francisco 49ers Part Ways With Veteran QB & Former UFL MV...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have made a move to solidify the most important position on the roster.

"The 49ers are releasing Adrian Martinez, going with Kurtis Rourke as QB3," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport wrote on his official X account on Saturday.

Martinez signed a reserve/futured contracts with the 49ers in January after spending the last part of the 2025 regular season with them. He was called out for his inaccuracy over the preseason — Martinez has mostly been known throughout his college and pro career as a running quarterback.

"49ers tight ends' and receivers' ribs aren't going to miss these Adrian Martinez throws," The Athletic's Vic Tafur wrote on X on August 27.

The 6-foot-2, 220-pound former Nebraska and Kansas State star went undrafted in 2023 and landed with the Detroit Lions as a rookie but was released as part of final roster cuts.

Martinez Bounced Back After UFL Star Turn

Martinez didn't sit on his laurels after being cut by the Lions.

He bounced back with the UFL's Birmingham Stallions in 2024, where he led his team to the UFL Championship, was named UFL MVP and UFL Championship Game MVP as well as leading the UFL in rushing yards.

That start turn propelled Martinez back to the NFL, where he spent 2024 and 2025 with the New York Jets .

Kurtis Rourke Seems Ready for Backup Role

Rourke was a 2-time All-MAC selection and the 2022 MAC Most Valuable Player at Ohio before transferring and leading the Hoosiers to a 10-1 record and the College Football Playoff in his first season as a starter in 2024.

Rourke, 6-foot-5 and 231 pounds, will turn 26 in October and started 45 games in college, with 10,144 career passing yards, 71 touchdowns and 20 interceptions. He also rushed for 816 yards and 13 touchdowns.

The 49ers drafted Rourke in the 7th round (No. 227 overall) of the 2025 NFL Draft.

The Ontario, Canada, native was also taken in the CFL Draft, in the 3rd round (No. 25 overall) by the Saskatchewan Roughriders.

"Rourke earns a draftable grade because of his size, experience and production," NFL draft analyst Lance Zierlein wrote in 2025. "He's coming off an ACL tear, but the injury might not have a major impact on his draft slotting since his game isn't built on mobility. Rourke's evaluation requires 2023 tape to get a feel for his delivery and velocity when his knee is stable. While he can make pro throws, the accuracy and placement is average. He's a decent field-reader who throws with adequate touch and anticipation. Rourke played winning football in 2024 and he's plenty tough, but he needs to take better care of the football if he wants to stick with an NFL team."
