articles.title: New Saints Trade Rumors on Spencer Rattler Interest Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints will keep quarterback Spencer Rattler despite receiving trade interest, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints will keep quarterback Spencer Rattler despite receiving trade interest, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

The Saints selected Rattler with a fifth-round pick in the 2024 NFL draft. He's played in 16 games (14 starts) over two seasons, completing 62.7 percent of his passes for 2,903 yards (6.0 yards per attempt), 12 touchdowns and 10 interceptions.

Rattler was the Saints' starting quarterback for the first eight games of the 2025 season, but he was benched for Tyler Shough at halftime of the team's 23-3 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Oct. 26.

Shough, a then-rookie selected in the second round of the 2025 NFL draft, finished the season strong and even got chosen as a finalist for the Associated Press Offensive Rookie of the Year award. So he entered the 2026 offseason as the Saints' clear QB1.

Rattler remains the Saints' backup QB , though, and remains under contract with the team through 2027 . Through three preseason games this year, Rattler completed 30-of-44 passes (68.2 percent) for 262 yards and an interception.

New Orleans, which ended the season with a promising 5-3 stretch after a 1-8 start, begins 2026 on Sunday, Sept. 13 at the Detroit Lions.

articles.title: What it’s like to live with – and lose – a loved one with CTE
articles.summary: Maura Horton read the latest stories, the ones detailing the startling research that as many as one in four NFL players could end up with CTE, and she knew what would happen next.
articles.body: Maura Horton read the latest stories, the ones detailing the startling research that as many as one in four NFL players could end up with CTE, and she knew what would happen next. People would talk about chronic traumatic encephalopathy that day and for a few days after. They’d debate whether kids should play the sport. They’d posit about what could be done and try to reconcile this country’s love affair with football with the mounting evidence that the cumulative hits throughout a career can shatter lives. And then inevitably and invariably, they’d move on to whatever came next in the news cycle. She didn’t blame them. It’s the nature of humanity, especially when something feels far removed from your everyday life. Only .023% of high school players get even a snap in the NFL. CTE is, thereby, a tragedy that happens to other people. Except it happened to Maura’s family, to her 58-year-old husband, Don, the father of her two daughters, Hadley and Libby. CTE was and is the “earthquake” that came into Maura’s life and upended the road map she had planned, that they all had planned. The long marriage, modeled after her parents’ 60-plus years of connection, and days in the stands watching Hadley play soccer and seeing Libby turn her analytical math brain into a successful career; the anticipated extraordinary walks down the aisle and the ordinary walks around the block; the chance to get old and creaky together. The simple yet profound opportunity to create a life all rerouted and ultimately destroyed. And Don Horton didn’t play in the NFL. He was an offensive lineman at Wittenberg University, a Division III school that has had its share of glory (five national titles and 799 wins) but so far off-Broadway that only true football loyalists would know of it. He is, then, not a number in the most recent study, and yet he died in May 2016, a postmortem study of his brain confirming the cause of death that his family accepted long before his passing. It is that gap – the chasm between everyday athletes and NFL stars, between cause and effect, between assistance and diagnosis – that Maura wants closed. “I’m always thankful that the reports are published and the research is ongoing,” Maura told CNN Sports. “But there is still so much missing. I want to be a conduit that helps open a dialogue to understanding. No one sees the aftermath. No one understands what it’s like on a day-to-day basis. You see these studies and then no one talks about it again until someone dies. “But this is an earthquake that shattered my family, and no one understands how shattering it is. I’m 10 years past and it’s still shattering us.” An identity shaped by football They told Don, a committed fitness buff who suddenly struggled to lift weights, that he had Parkinson’s Disease. Maura laughs as she remembers the diagnosis, how people told her that of all the neurological disorders to have, this one was the most manageable. “Michael J. Fox,” she said. “Everyone brought up Michael J. Fox.” Yet Don’s health declined rapidly, and in ways that made Maura question the diagnosis. One day he’d be in the gym working out; and the next day he’d fall down for no reason. He had mood swings and fitful nights sleeping, bouts of paranoia and even hallucinations. Maura thought maybe it was the medications, and so she became her husband’s self-appointed pit bull, going to doctor’s visits to pepper the physicians with questions. She also researched on the side and as Don’s condition continued to deteriorate, she wondered if maybe he had CTE. Finally, she direct messaged Chris Nowinski, the co-founder of the Boston-based Concussion Legacy Foundation. Maura then spoke to Don about donating his brain to science after he died. He balked. Here was a man who devoted his life to healthy living. He eschewed junk food and regularly hit the gym, and yet his wife was suggesting to him that there was nothing he could do or have done, that a decision he made as a kid put him on a path he couldn’t prevent. That football did this to him. The game was as much who Don was as what he did. He jumped right into coaching after his playing career ended, beginning the sojourner football life that took him from various stops in Ohio to New Mexico and Virginia. In 1997, he hit the big time, landing a gig as the offensive line coach at Boston College. He’d spend 10 years with the Eagles before finishing his career at N.C. State. Considering – let alone accepting – that the sport that gave him purpose and direction, the one he used as a foundational guide for the hundreds of young men he coached, was his undoing felt impossible. Like he was not only betraying football, but the men he recruited to play it as well. But as his condition deteriorated, he reluctantly agreed. “Mostly,” Maura says, “because he wanted to prove me wrong.” ‘Parented by a ghost’ Hadley Horton is only 18 and she’s already made a TED Talk. Crafted via TEDEd, her “Grief, Joy and the Magic in Between” talks about her beloved Elf on the Shelf, Tommy, who she used to write to as a child. The conversations used to be silly, targeted entirely around the holidays, but Tommy eventually became a pen pal and even a therapy chair, Hadley often sending notes off to the North Pole long after Santa’s work for the season was done. Eventually she discovered, via the Notes app on Maura’s phone, that her mom was Tommy. “Through letters and tiny acts of care, she taught me that love doesn’t always announce itself; sometimes it quietly anchors you,” Hadley says in the talk. “When I reflect on Tommy’s impact on my life, I understand that that belief in something bigger than yourself can often times get you through difficult times.” This is half of what Maura wants people to understand; that there are people behind the statistics, that there are children who have grown up without a father and spouses who saw their life upended, never to be righted again. And it is not just NFL players. It is kids whose dads played college ball or even stopped in high school after having their bell rung one too many times. “It’s like they’re still being parented by a ghost,” she said. Yet as Maura navigated her new normal, she realized quickly that the resources available to families faced with similarly grim diagnoses weren’t there for her. CTE, instead, is always about the after, about the postmortem brain study that confirms the presence of the disease. Except, it’s in the during that people need help. When Don was intitally diagnosed with Parkinson’s, he and Maura immediately scrolled to the Michael J. Fox Foundation. They found scads of information about medication and care, and research for a cure. In a powerless situation, it felt empowering to grab hold of something that could better their lives. But when Maura began to suspect CTE, she found considerably less information. There is the organization that Nowinski founded and one other, Concussion to Empowerment. She attended one family summit and struggled to find any advice about medication or treatment. She even questioned why, when Don first went in with his symptoms, no one thought to ask if he played football, to at least put CTE into the equation. More, she realized, he was one of thousands – countless college football players and guys who stopped after high school; military members and soccer players – who used their heads as battering rams. Her own daughter, Hadley, played soccer and continues to play at the collegiate level. Ten months after her husband’s death, the CTE Center and Concussion Legacy Foundation confirmed what Maura already knew; Don had CTE. The disease is graded for severity, with four being the worst. Don was somewhere between a three and four. “He didn’t play in the NFL; he didn’t have a pension plan,” she said. “It wasn’t like he had protection or resources or a community around us to help navigate. It always felt like I was in fight mode. There is so much room for growth. It’s like if you compare it to Mothers Against Drunk Driving, there’s no education component. It’s just, ‘go play flag football.’” ‘It happened to us’ Maura still loves football. She still watches it, still supports the former players and other coaches Don worked with. It is, as it always was, part of her fall schedule. But when she’s asked what she would say to a young mother who was weighing to let her child play, she pauses. She talks about parental motivation, about the hope that one’s child can find the value of teamwork and enjoy the camaraderie and life lessons of sport and wonders out loud if maybe it’s not worth considering another sport instead. “There are so many choices,” she says. “Because that’s the problem. So much of the conversation centers around the NFL; people can’t conceptualize that it can happen to their family. That’s what really needs to change. “People think that because they’re not part of that world, it’s not about them. Well, we weren’t either, and it happened to us.”

articles.title: 2026 Fantasy Football 4-Round Mock Draft, Top Keeper Players and Team Names
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL preseason is complete and cutdown day has arrived. Naturally, this means that it's time to dive head-first into fantasy football drafts.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL preseason is complete and cutdown day has arrived. Naturally, this means that it's time to dive head-first into fantasy football drafts.

Ideally, the preseason has provided some insight into what roles players are projected to fill in 2026 and how they should be valued on draft day. However, that's only part of the equation.

Knowing when to target specific players, which top 2025 performers should be retained in keeper leagues, and what to name teams in 2026 can help put the finishing touches on that championship squad. Fortunately, we're here to help.

All rankings, picks, and analysis here is based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, Seattle Seahawks

Christian McCaffrey, RB, San Francisco 49ers

Omarion Hampton, RB, Los Angeles Chargers

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Kansas City Chiefs

Tetairoa McMillan, WR, Carolina Panthers

Jayden Daniels, QB, Washington Commanders

Terry McLaurin, WR, Washington Commanders

Successfully navigating a keeper draft requires more than just knowing who your top performers from the previous season were and then holding onto them. Managers must weigh the value of potential keepers against the value of players they expect to be available while also factoring in boom-or-bust potential.

This is obviously a tricky process since managers usually won't know which players their opponents are keeping—some leagues will post an active keepers list ahead of draft day. However, diving into rosters can help.

If, for example, one of your opponents has Bijan Robinson, CeeDee Lamb, and Ashton Jeanty on their roster, they're going to have to part with one top-10 player in a traditional keeper league. If your roster has no top-10 players, it could be beneficial to eschew keepers entirely in order to try landing one.

Conversely, keeping two top-10 players should be an easy decision. Since keeper picks take the place of first- and second-round draft choices, you're probably going to find more value in keeping, say, Jahmyr Gibbs and James Cook than you'll find by keeping just Gibbs and using that second-round pick.

Risk management should also be a component of the keeper process. Older players or those with a history of injuries—such as Christian McCaffrey and Joe Burrow—could be top-tier performers in 2026 but could also bust in a big way. If you believe you can find safer picks in the first two rounds, it's better to re-draft than retain risk-reward players.

articles.title: New Aaron Donald Rumors on Return, Contract Leak Ahead of Rams' NFL Opener vs. 49ers in Australia
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams "are still optimistic" about a possible return by three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams "are still optimistic" about a possible return by three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

Fowler reported Sunday on SportsCenter the situation remains fluid as the Rams prepare for their opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia. Should Donald decide to come back, L.A. will then focus on the financial particulars:

"He's had several workouts with the team that they've had to list as like a free-agent workout. He's done that. Still no firm answer, but there's not a huge rush here. I've never really sensed that because they know Aaron Donald keeps himself in phenomenal shape. He can come in as an in-season sniper. You know, he doesn't have to play the 17 games. They're getting ready to go to Australia. Now, there is still time. They're leaving late in the process, just a few days before that next Thursday. So, still some time if he wants to get signed and get acclimated. He's also got his contract. He's got one year, $30 million that's frozen from his previous contract when he retired. Do they need to re that up? They're sort of waiting for him to decide, 'Do I definitely want to play?' Once he does that, then they can address his contract. "

The MMQB's Albert Breer said earlier this week on The Rich Eisen Show that Donald's contract for 2026 could present a hurdle. The Rams are $16.7 million under the salary cap, half as much as he's entitled to earn.

Even assuming the 35-year-old takes a pay cut, it could have a domino effect. Adding void years to a reworked contract would impact the cap beyond this season, for example.

Wide receiver Puka Nacua and defenders Kobie Turner and Byron Young are among the Rams' notable free agents in 2027, so general manager Les Snead will want to have as much long-term flexibility as possible.

The opportunity to add Donald is tough to pass up. Given both his likely role and the way in which he has taken care of his body should make it easier to work him into the lineup after Week 1 if it comes to that.

Settling on a contract number that works for everybody could prove to be the sticking point.

articles.title: Is Travis Kelce preparing to leave the NFL behind? Inside his $90 million empire and business moves
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce is approaching another important season with the Kansas City Chiefs, but his biggest moves may be happening away from the football field..
articles.body: Travis Kelce is approaching another important season with the Kansas City Chiefs, but his biggest moves may be happening away from the football field. With retirement questions surrounding the veteran tight end, his growing work in media, entertainment, endorsements and business has created a strong second act. His reported $90 million net worth also means Kelce has built financial options that could soften the impact of eventually leaving the NFL.Travis Kelce's business empire extends beyond the NFLKelce has spent years turning his popularity as an NFL star into opportunities outside football. His biggest media venture remains New Heights, the podcast he hosts with his brother, Jason Kelce. The show has grown into a major entertainment property, attracting a huge audience through conversations about football, family and life away from the field.The brothers strengthened that business in 2024 when they agreed to a reported deal with Amazon's Wondery worth more than $100 million over three years. The agreement gave New Heights a much larger commercial platform and showed how valuable the Kelce brothers' combined appeal had become.Kelce has also moved deeper into television and film. His acting work includes Grotesquerie and Happy Gilmore 2. He also took on hosting duties for Are You Smarter Than a Celebrity?Those projects matter because they give Kelce experience in an industry where his NFL career is not the deciding factor. He can build on his personality, name recognition and ability to connect with audiences, even after his playing days end.Endorsements and investments add another layer to the picture. Kelce has become one of the NFL's most marketable stars, allowing him to work with major brands while exploring business opportunities away from the Chiefs.Travis Kelce retirement questions grow ahead of 2026 seasonDespite his expanding business interests, Kelce has not confirmed that he will retire after the 2026 NFL season. For now, his attention remains on football and another run with Kansas City.Still, the possibility of retirement is becoming harder to ignore. Kelce has openly admitted that the question is something he considers regularly.“I think about it every single day,” Kelce previously said when discussing retirement. “It’s a decision that I’m going to have to make at some point.”That statement offers a glimpse into the reality facing a player who has spent more than a decade at the highest level. Football demands a huge physical commitment, and Kelce has already enjoyed a career most players can only dream about.Yet his passion for the sport remains clear.“I love football,” Kelce has said. “I love coming into work every single day.”That could be why his business expansion should not automatically be viewed as a sign that he is ready to walk away. Instead, Kelce appears to be building a future while continuing to compete in the present.With a reported net worth of around $90 million and a portfolio spanning podcasting, entertainment, endorsements and investments, Kelce has already laid much of the groundwork for life after football. Whether 2026 becomes his final season with the Chiefs remains unknown. articles.title: Bears & Falcons Make Surprise Trade for Key DT Starter, NFL Rumors on Full Return Before Roster Cuts
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears are trading defensive tackle Gervon Dexter to the Atlanta Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a fifth-round draft pick, according to Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN and NFL Network.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears are trading defensive tackle Gervon Dexter to the Atlanta Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a fifth-round draft pick, according to Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN and NFL Network.

Dexter started all 17 games for the Bears in 2025, finishing with 44 combined tackles and six sacks. He's entering the final year of his rookie contract, and the Bears clearly had reservations about extending him beyond 2026.

His exit also comes after coach Ben Johnson heaped a ton of praise on sixth-round draft pick Jordan van den Berg. He called van den Berg "an incredible athlete" earlier this week.

"He's still learning the game of football to a degree, and yet it's amazing what he brings to the table," Johnson told reporters . "He's been the same guy every single day. Smile on his face. He loves football. He loves the process. I haven't seen it yet, but someone told me he was mic'ed up in that first game and he's coming to the sideline, he's talking to [defensive tackle] Grady [Jarrett] about the things that are happening on the field. Grady's helping him, giving him tidbits here and there. It's a good thing to see right now. He's firmly in the mix."

It appears van den Berg will be occupying a big role along the defensive line.

Phillips brings some depth to the secondary, though he's coming off a season in which a triceps injury limited him to one game.

The Falcons, meanwhile, are getting an immediate upgrade to their defensive front. They signed Da'Shawn Hand to a team-friendly one-year deal , but he has missed time this offseason through injury.

General manager Ian Cunningham has some added familiarity with Dexter as well. He was in Chicago's front office when the Bears drafted him in 2023.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on 'Rare' Decision Browns Eye with Shedeur Sanders, Watson, Gabriel, Taylen Green
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns' quarterback room could go four-deep heading into the 2026 NFL regular season, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns' quarterback room could go four-deep heading into the 2026 NFL regular season, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

Fowler said Sunday on SportsCenter that "there is certainly a scenario" where the Browns keep Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green all on their final roster.

The NFL insider suggested it's "pretty rare" for a team to keep four active QBs, though the Pittsburgh Steelers appear to be headed in that direction as well.

Watson and Sanders were effectively locks to make the final cut before the offseason got underway. Releasing Watson would require eating a lot of dead money , while Sanders warranted more time to develop after he started seven games as a rookie.

That seemingly left Gabriel as the odd man out, especially when considering Cleveland used a sixth-round pick on Green.

The southpaw looked good in a 37-13 win over the New England Patriots, though. He finished 12-of-15 for 186 yards and three touchdowns.

The preseason finale was Green's only action. He was 5-of-7 for 27 yards and ran for 66 yards on eight carries.

The obvious question is what Cleveland has to gain by holding onto both Gabriel and Green when neither seriously challenged Sanders for the backup role.

ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi made the case for having four quarterbacks.

"However, Cleveland is effectively using Green's rookie season as a redshirt year," he wrote. "And between Watson's struggles, injury history and the reception from the home crowd in the second preseason game — he was met with loud boos — the Browns might opt to keep Gabriel on the 53-man roster as another backup option."

In the case of Gabriel, signaling that you intend to roster him could boost his trade market that little bit more. Flipping him for a late-round draft pick is better than cutting him for nothing.

Ultimately, the question for the Browns is whether anybody emerges as a suitable QB solution beyond 2026. The depth chart is going to look a lot different in 2027 if none of Watson, Sanders or Gabriel provides signs of encouragement.

articles.title: New J.J. McCarthy Trade Rumors Leak as Vikings Eye Roster Cuts After QB Demoted Behind Kyler, Wentz
articles.summary: It wasn't long ago the Minnesota Vikings surely saw J.J. McCarthy as a franchise building block after selecting him with the No. 10 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft, but the quarterback's future with the team is reportedly in the air going into his third season.
articles.body:
It wasn't long ago the Minnesota Vikings surely saw J.J. McCarthy as a franchise building block after selecting him with the No. 10 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft, but the quarterback's future with the team is reportedly in the air going into his third season.

"I've called around the league on trade possibilities for backup quarterbacks, his name really didn't come up a lot yesterday and this morning," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Sunday on SportsCenter . "But they have Carson Wentz, who was one of their backups last time. So they want to make Wentz the two and McCarthy the three, or do they want to move on? That's sort of the question that looms around the league right now."

With Kyler Murray already established as the starter , the Vikings have until Sunday's 6 p.m. ET roster cut deadline to decide whether they will cut McCarthy if they cannot find a trade.

The writing seemed to be on the wall for McCarthy's future as the Vikings' starter when they brought in Murray during the offseason.

Yes, there was a quarterback competition during training camp. But a team that truly believes in its top-10 draft pick as the quarterback for the next decade-plus likely wouldn't have brought in such an established name to compete.

Murray himself is looking to bounce back after injuries limited him to just five games last season and eight games in 2023. Still, he was a back-to-back Pro Bowler during the 2020 and 2021 campaigns and could elevate the team's offense simply by being an average quarterback.

And that may be all he needs to do given the overall talent surrounding him on a roster that includes Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, Aaron Jones and T.J. Hockenson, among others.

Minnesota managed to go 9-8 last season while rotating through McCarthy, Wentz and Max Brosmer under center. That is not exactly a list of All-Pro candidates, but the talent around the signal-caller gave the team a high floor.

McCarthy completed just 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions last season. His QBR of 35.6 was 30th in the league, per Pro Football Reference , and his inconsistency may have cost the Vikings a playoff spot.

Not only that, it may have cost him a roster spot depending on what the NFC North team wants to do Sunday with Murray and Wentz as other options at the position.

articles.title: New Odell Beckham Jr. Rumors on NFL Future, Potential Fantasy Role as Giants Eye Roster Cuts
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. reportedly has the inside track for a roster spot with the New York Giants ahead of Sunday's 6 p.m. ET cut deadline.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. reportedly has the inside track for a roster spot with the New York Giants ahead of Sunday's 6 p.m. ET cut deadline.

"It looks like he played his way into a spot on the Giants' 53-man roster," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Sunday on SportsCenter . "Not solidified yet; John Harbaugh, the head coach, has not tipped his hand. But they've had some injuries to the position. He's held up pretty well. I talked to a team source who said if Odell Beckham embraces being a complementary piece and no longer the man, he can really help the Giants because he can still play, he can still get open."

While fantasy football managers may not love the idea of Beckham being "a complementary piece," it is a testament to the veteran he is in such a position to make the roster given the injuries he has overcome.

Beckham helped lead the Los Angeles Rams to the Lombardi Trophy during the 2021 campaign but suffered a torn ACL during the Super Bowl win. He then missed the 2022 season before he was limited to nine games in 2024.

He also didn't play during the 2025 season and had to clarify he wasn't retiring .

So fantasy football managers may not want to count on the 33-year-old as a top wide-receiver option, but he showed enough during training camp to impress Harbaugh enough to make the roster.

"I think he has done enough to make an NFL roster for sure," Harbaugh said Friday. "He's played well. He's gotten better as camp's gone along, and I think he deserves credit for that."

Making the Giants of all teams would be a full-circle moment for the LSU product.

New York selected him with the No. 12 overall pick of the 2014 NFL draft, and he quickly became one of the league's top playmakers as the Offensive Rookie of the Year and a Pro Bowler in his first season. In fact, he made the Pro Bowl in each of his first three seasons while finishing with more than 1,300 receiving yards in all of them.

While Beckham has bounced around to the Cleveland Browns, Rams, Baltimore Ravens and Miami Dolphins, he is best remembered for his individual dominance on the Giants.

He won't be challenging for 1,300 yards again in 2026 on a depth chart with Malik Nabers, Darnell Mooney and Darius Slayton, but he is in a position to take advantage of single coverage with opposing defenses focused on Nabers in particular and help the team that drafted him compete in the NFC East.

articles.title: Bills Trade 2x CFP National Champion OL to Colts, Latest Details on Return Ahead of NFL Roster Cuts
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills traded interior offensive lineman Sedrick Van Pran-Granger to the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills traded interior offensive lineman Sedrick Van Pran-Granger to the Indianapolis Colts.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero first reported the trade.

Van Pran-Granger made 31 appearances in two years with Buffalo. A fifth-round pick in the 2024 NFL draft, he won a pair of national titles at Georgia.

David Benjamin De Cristofaro of Bills Wire posited earlier this week that Van Pran-Granger might be on the bubble: "Lloyd Cushenberry was [coach Joe] Brady's center during the famous 2019 season at LSU, and has been taking the snaps in starting center Connor McGovern's absence as he works his way back to the field from injury. The team also signed Sincere Haynesworth this week, perhaps forecasting a move."

A sixth-round pick isn't a massive return, but it's something of value for a player who may not have made Buffalo's final roster.

For Van Pran-Granger, landing in Indy effectively cements him as the backup center, a role that wasn't assured for him on the Bills.

The Colts will roll into 2026 with Tanor Bortolini as the starter after he appeared in all but one of their games at center a season ago. Behind him, however, the preseason was a terrible audition for Dalton Tucker.

Going from Tucker to Van Pran-Granger will solidify Indianapolis' depth in the middle of the line as the team prepares to face off with the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 13 in Week 1.

articles.title: Colts receiver Keenan Allen arrested on charges of driving while intoxicated
articles.summary: The arrest occurred in downtown Indianapolis at approximately 1 a.m., according to local police reports.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts receiver Keenan Allen was arrested early Sunday morning for allegedly driving while intoxicated, according to local police reports.

Allen, 34, was arrested in downtown Indianapolis at approximately 1 a.m. on preliminary charges of DWI and DWI endangering a person, as reported by FOX59 . Both are misdemeanor charges.

Allen was arrested with a blood alcohol content of 0.08 or more, according to the Indianapolis Metro Police Department. As of Sunday morning, Allen is being held at the Marion County Jail, the Indianapolis Star reports .

Officers approached Allen's car when they noticed it parked in a no-parking zone, according to the IMPD report (via FOX59). While speaking with Allen, they noticed signs of intoxication and he was subsequently arrested.

"We are aware of the incident involving Keenan Allen last night," the Colts said in a statement, via ESPN. "We are in the process of gathering more information and have no further comment at this time."

Allen signed a one-year contract with the Colts on Aug. 19 that could be worth up to $8.32 million. He made his preseason debut in Saturday's 25-16 loss to the Detroit Lions, catching one pass for 24 yards from quarterback Anthony Richardson on the team's first series. That was his only target for the game.

In 13 NFL seasons, Allen has 1.055 receptions for 12,051 yards and 70 touchdowns. A six-time Pro Bowl selection, he has surpassed 1,000 or more receiving yards six times during his career and tallied at least 100 receptions five times.

Allen's best season was 2017, when he caught 102 passes for 1,393 yards and 6 TDs with the then-San Diego Chargers. A 2013 third-round pick (No. 76 overall) by the Chargers, he played 13 seasons with the team and one with the Chicago Bears after a 2024 trade.

articles.title: Bucs Make Decision on QB2 amid Baker Mayfield's Contract Negotiations, New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have reportedly settled on their backup quarterback.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have reportedly settled on their backup quarterback.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Jalon Daniels will back up Baker Mayfield—who has an uncertain long-term future with the team because of his own contract situation—to start the 2026 campaign.

Daniels joined the Buccaneers as an undrafted free agent with a signing bonus of $25,000, but Rapoport noted he "impressed throughout camp" and "earned" the role.

Tampa Bay signed Jake Browning this offseason after he started 10 games for the Cincinnati Bengals the past three seasons when Joe Burrow was injured. Browning was presumably going to be Mayfield's backup just like he was for Burrow in Cincinnati but was unable to beat out Daniels for the job.

However, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Browning was released Sunday with Daniels as the backup moving forward.

While Daniels dealt with injuries early in his collegiate career with Kansas even amid a breakout 2022 campaign, he appeared in 12 games in each of the last two seasons for the Jayhawks.

He posted 14 touchdown passes to 12 interceptions in 2024 but showed significant improvement in 2025 while completing 62.1 percent of his passes for 2,531 yards, 22 touchdowns and seven interceptions to go with 404 yards and four scores on the ground.

Daniels earned praise for his leadership and work ethic at Kansas and wasted little time proving himself at the NFL level with Tampa Bay by earning the backup role despite joining the team as an undrafted free agent.

The signal-caller saw time in each of the NFC South team's three preseason games and performed as follows:

It wasn't just the passing, as he also ran for a touchdown during the win over the Jets.

As for Mayfield, the 2026 campaign is the final one on his contract. He said he plans on focusing on football during the season after he and the Buccaneers were unable to come to terms on a long-term deal, but there remains plenty of uncertainty.

But there is no longer uncertainty over who is going to be his backup when Tampa Bay opens the season against the Bengals on Sept. 13 at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: “We are changing lives..Truly a blessing”: How Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes turned a $1.077M gift into hope for 20 Kansas City charities and children in need
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has built much of his legacy on football fields, but his work away from the game has become just as meaningful. In Oct. 2024, the Kans.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has built much of his legacy on football fields, but his work away from the game has become just as meaningful. In Oct. 2024, the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, brought their 15 and the Mahomies Foundation gala back to Kansas City for its fifth annual edition. More than 850 supporters attended the event, helping the foundation grant $1.077 million to 20 Kansas City charities.For Brittany, the night was about more than the money raised. It was about being able to give back to a community that has become such an important part of the Mahomes family's life. After the gala, she shared her gratitude on Instagram, describing the opportunity to help local communities as “truly a blessing.” The message captured why the couple has continued putting their platform behind causes that can give children better opportunities. How did Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes turn one night into a major Kansas City investment?The fifth annual 15 and the Mahomies Foundation gala brought together hundreds of people to support causes across Kansas City. By the end of the evening, $1,077,000 had been granted to 20 local charities, giving the event an impact that stretched well beyond the ballroom.The foundation highlighted the support in a post following the gala, thanking the more than 850 people who attended and the partners who helped make the event possible. The organization said the supporters continued to take the event “to a new level each year” and added, “Together, we are changing lives. Let’s keep it rolling!”Brittany shared the same sense of gratitude when she reflected on the event. “Truly a blessing to be able to make an impact in these communities!” she wrote.That message was important because the Mahomes family has made Kansas City a central part of its charitable work. The 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, which Patrick founded in 2019, is focused on improving the lives of children through initiatives connected to health, wellness and communities.The 2024 gala also followed another major fundraising event earlier that year. Patrick and Brittany hosted their 15 and the Mahomies Foundation Golf Classic in Las Vegas in April, where the couple was joined by Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift. Swift donated Eras Tour tickets to the auction, and the tickets eventually sold for $80,000. Brittany later called the night “Epic” while thanking everyone who supported the foundation. Why was the Mahomes family's $1.625 million commitment an even bigger step?The Kansas City gala was not an isolated act of generosity. A year earlier, Patrick and Brittany announced a much larger commitment that showed how seriously they viewed their role in supporting children.In October 2023, their foundation partnered with Boys & Girls Clubs of America and pledged $1.625 million as part of a multi-year commitment. The money was directed toward young people in communities that held personal meaning for the couple, including Greater Kansas City, Lubbock, Tyler and Whitehouse, Texas.The connection was especially personal. Whitehouse is where Patrick attended high school, while Brittany had experience with a Boys & Girls Club during her childhood. The partnership was designed to provide children with better access to safe spaces, mentors, programs and other resources.Patrick explained why the partnership mattered to him, saying, “Kids who attend a Club, like Brittany once did, are provided with the necessary tools and resources to help this generation not only thrive but lead with compassion and purpose.”He also described the partnership as an investment in children, saying, “We are truly excited to partner with Boys & Girls Clubs of America by investing in the future of children.”That same commitment was reflected in Brittany's words. She said, “This meaningful partnership will expand opportunities for kids everywhere, and the places that have positively impacted Patrick and me. We are committed to doing all we can to uplift others.”The $1.077 million raised at the 2024 gala therefore fits into a much larger pattern. Patrick and Brittany have continued using their success to support children and communities, whether through major partnerships, local grants or fundraising events.For the Mahomes family, the goal has never been limited to one night or one donation. Their work has increasingly focused on creating opportunities that can stay with children long after the cameras leave. articles.title: Cowboys & Steelers Make Surprise Trade, Latest Details on Return Ahead of Roster Cuts Deadline
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers moved on from offensive tackle Broderick Jones by trading him to the Dallas Cowboys ahead of the final season of his expiring rookie contract.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers moved on from offensive tackle Broderick Jones by trading him to the Dallas Cowboys ahead of the final season of his expiring rookie contract.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and Jeremy Fowler first reported the details on Saturday.

The Cowboys also released wide receiver Denzel Mims Saturday, according to Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News.

The moves come after Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday outside linebacker Marist Liufau had suffered a fractured forearm necessitating surgery.

The Cowboys could use one of two IR spots for Liufau if he is expected to miss at least the first four games of the season.

Jones, the No. 14 pick of the 2023 draft, played the first three seasons of his NFL career for the Steelers.

He started 11 games in 2025 before he was shut down for the season with a neck injury.

Jones arrives in Dallas having played in 45 games with 38 career starts for the Steelers.

The Steelers declined the fifth-year option on Jones' rookie contract earlier this spring.

The decision took place after Schefter reported in April that Jones had suffered a "setback" in his recovery from his neck injury.

Jones was sidelined for most of the offseason. He was cleared in time for training camp but struggled at points in the preseason, including when he gave up two sacks in an Aug. 21 matchup against the New York Jets.

Jones started the 2025 campaign as the Steelers' starting left tackle, but that position was taken when the team moved Troy Fautanu to left tackle earlier this offseason.

The Steelers also drafted right tackle Max Iheanachor in the first round of the 2026 draft, further calling into question Jones' future with the team.

The Cowboys currently have Tyler Guyton seemingly as a lock at left tackle. Jones could potentially provide some competition for Terence Steele at right tackle once he arrives in Dallas.

The NFL roster cutdown deadline is Sunday at 6 p.m. ET. The Cowboys will need to decide where Jones fits in the team's tackle depth chart before opening the season Sept. 13 at the New York Giants.

articles.title: Cardinals Make Surprise Trade for Jaguars TE After Trey McBride's Back-to-Back NFL Pro Bowls
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars reportedly made a trade ahead of Sunday's 6 p.m. ET roster cut deadline.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars reportedly made a trade ahead of Sunday's 6 p.m. ET roster cut deadline.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo reported the Jaguars sent tight end Hunter Long to the Arizona Cardinals.

The 28-year-old, who entered the league as a third-round pick in 2021, figures to provide depth behind back-to-back Pro Bowler Trey McBride.

McBride is one of the best tight ends in the league and figures to draw the majority of the attention from opposing defenses. Perhaps that could open Long up in two-tight-end sets to become more productive after he was not much of a contributor during his first five seasons.

The Boston College product has bounced around from the Miami Dolphins to the Los Angeles Rams to the Jaguars and had just eight total catches in his first four years in the league.

However, the 2025 season in Jacksonville was his most productive, as he tallied 12 catches for 85 yards and two touchdowns.

Despite that slight uptick in production, there likely wasn't a significant role waiting for him with the Jaguars in 2026. Brenton Strange is the starter, and the AFC South team selected both Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol in the 2026 NFL draft.

Jacksonville surely wants to see what it has in the rookies and moved on from Long.

Yet it was able to find a trade partner in the Cardinals, which means it got something back in return instead of just releasing Long ahead of the roster cut deadline.

articles.title: Eagles News: Philadelphia’s most likely first-time Pro Bowl candidate
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 8/30/26.
articles.body:
Let's get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

One potential first-time Pro Bowler from each NFC team heading into the 2026 NFL season – NFL.com A.J. Brown's exit opens a trove of opportunities for DeVonta Smith. Yes, the Eagles drafted Makai Lemon in the first round and buffered the unit with veterans, but Smith is the alpha. The sixth-year pro boasts route-running ability and can generate separation with the best of them. Smith is a WR1. There will be no question now. [BLG Note: Isn't it wild how DeVonta hasn't made a Pro Bowl already? He's certainly that caliber of player.]

A thought on all 90 Eagles leaving 2026 training camp – NBCSP WR DeVonta Smith: The Eagles were without Smith for a good portion of this training camp as he healed from a hamstring injury but they're very excited to see him take over as their WR1. A.J. Brown was a great player in Philly but his absence will open the door for Smith to have a huge season in an expanded role. When he has been on the field, we've seen how good Smith can be. What really stood out this summer was his ability to bring in contested catches against some really good cornerbacks. Smith should shine in Sean Mannion's offense.

Eagles-Bengals snap counts: Cole Payton saw some special teams action – BGN The Eagles experimented with using Cole Payton on punt coverage. He finished the summer with just 21 preseason snaps, 15 of which came in his encouraging NFL debut. Weird and disappointing that the Eagles didn't make a better effort to get him more experience after that, unless they're just trying to prevent other teams from poaching him? But maybe just play him and then keep him on your roster? Seems like a wasted developmental opportunity.

NFL Rookie of the Year 2026 predictions, including one 3rd round sleeper – SB Nation Makai Lemon, WR — Philadelphia Eagles. Lemon is sitting at WR3 on the Eagles depth chart, which is the role he was drafted for. Working out of the slot in this offense will give him a lot of opportunities, and Philly brings the exposure needed to build a campaign. Lemon is also in a position where he could get a lot of targets from Jalen Hurts, and is in a rare situation among the rookie receivers where he's landing on an elite offense. There's a chance he could become a key touchdown scorer this season, and I'm not entirely sure that being on an offense with DeVonta Smith will really hurt him.

Eagles worked out an intriguing edge defender; Cowboys made a weird trade – PhillyVoice Reiger was a priority undrafted free agent who signed with the Miami Dolphins. Leading up to the draft, most analysts thought he would be selected. For example, he was Mel Kiper's 140th-ranked (4th/5th round) prospect, and Dane Brugler's 197th-ranked (5th/6th round) prospect. But, Reiger had a complicated evaluation because of a worrisome injury history, as noted in Brugler's scouting report.

Preseason Football – Iggles Blitz Na Brown. Paul Turner. And now Carson Steele. He was released by the Eagles and that confused more than a few people. You can argue he was the best Eagles player over the past two games. But that was in terms of results, not process. Steele has the right combination of size, athleticism and effort that helps him shine in August. He's done that with multiple teams. KC put him on the roster in 2024. He ran for 183 yards and averaged 3.3 yards per carry. He caught 7 passes and averaged 3.7 yards per reception. Not ideal. He's just not quite good enough to make plays against starters. Steele is great in the summer when he's going against future car salesmen, insurance employees or welders. He's not the same when going against guys like Zack Baun.

12 NFL teams did not play their starting quarterbacks in the preseason – PFT The growing trend of NFL teams keeping their quarterbacks out of the preseason has reached the point where more than one-third of starting quarterbacks did not take a single snap in this year's preseason. [BLG Note: Jalen Hurts was obviously one of these 12.]

Eagles' Cooper DeJean attends Red Bull Championship Run in Philadelphia – CBS News At the Red Bull Championship Run, 120 contestants tried to retrieve a flag at the end of a 30-foot greased pole over the Delaware River.

Falcons 2026 roster cut tracker – The Falcoholic [Former Eagles UDFA signing] G Jaeden Roberts

Carolina Panthers 2026 roster cuts tracker – Cat Scratch Reader [Former Eagle] Elijah Cooks, wide receiver

BREAKING: Cowboys trade with Steelers for OT Broderick Jones – Blogging The Boys Jones was not regarded well by Steelers fans, so this is something that they are celebrating with vigor. The Cowboys needed help at tackle as noted, but did they need help this badly?

2026 NFL offseason trade grades: Gervon Dexter, Broderick Jones – ESPN The Steelers got a solid return for a player they could have feasibly cut on Sunday — that's always good business on cut-down day. Though, it is a little scary to walk into Week 1 with poor tackle depth behind Iheanachor and left tackle Troy Fautanu, both of whom have injury histories. The Cowboys take a big swing on a talented athlete at a position in which they have had some instability, and returning Jones to the right could help him return to his previous form of play. The Cowboys have yet to confirm which side is the plan for Jones, as left tackle Tyler Guyton started the year in a camp competition but reportedly impressed with a great summer, while right tackle Terence Steele — a long-time starter under contract through 2028 — hasn't had the best play in past seasons. Ostensibly, Jones is better on the right and has a better path to reps on the right … but the recent film and injury history is scary to buy into, no matter the side.

Commanders vs. Ravens preseason Week 3: Mark Tyler's Studs and Duds – Hogs Haven OL Julian Good-Jones. Living up to the moniker I have bestowed upon him, "Bad-Jones" was every bit as bad as you could expect. It's absolutely crazy to think that if Washington had a regular-season game tomorrow, this man may be our starting center. Shame, SHAME on Adam Peters!

Giants-Jets winners and losers: Odell Beckham makes his case – Big Blue View Odell Beckham Jr. — Is anyone still questioning whether or not Beckham is making the 53-man roster? Beckham nearly had a 73-yard touchdown reception, but Jameis Winston slightly overthrew him and the ball fell incomplete. Beckham still had an outstanding night. He caught three passes for 53 yards, an average of 17.7 yards per catch, with the longest being a 23-yard grab. He has enough juice to be a useful player for this Giants team. John Harbaugh said after the game that Beckham has done enough to make a roster, but stopped short of anointing him as part of the Giants' 53-man roster.

articles.title: Chiefs face critical 2026 season with Patrick Mahomes returning from ACL tear
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes faces a critical recovery from his ACL tear as the Kansas City Chiefs try to bounce back from a disastrous 6-11 season in 2025.
articles.body: When a dominant modern dynasty experiences a sudden, injury-plagued collapse, determining whether it was a minor blip or the start of a decline becomes the paramount question for bettors. Few teams in the NFL find themselves under as unique a spotlight entering this season as the Kansas City Chiefs. Last Year The Chiefs suffered a nightmare 2025 campaign, stumbling to a 6–11 record and missing the postseason for the first time since 2014. Kansas City showed flashes of its championship pedigree, stringing together hard-fought victories early in the fall. However, the team went a brutal 1–9 in one-score games, plagued by self-inflicted mistakes, road struggles, and a devastating six-game losing streak to close out the year. The tipping point arrived in Week 15 when Patrick Mahomes suffered a season-ending ACL tear. The season was over by that point anyway, but it put their hopes for this season in serious jeopardy. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Offseason additions and subtractions The front office focused on reloading the offense and retooling a depleted secondary. On offense, Kansas City made a splash in free agency by signing explosive running back Kenneth Walker III to a three-year deal, alongside re-signing cornerstone tight end Travis Kelce to a three-year extension and extending Mahomes through 2033. To address defensive depth, they added safety Alohi Gilman, defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga, and cornerbacks Kader Kohou and Kaiir Elam, while bringing back L'Jarius Sneed on a one-year deal and picking up defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah. SUPER BOWL MVP KENNETH WALKER MISSES SEAHAWKS' RING CEREMONY AFTER SIGNING $45M DEAL WITH CHIEFS The additions did come with the sacrifice of some strong players. The secondary lost major pillars, as cornerback Trent McDuffie was traded to the Rams, and safety Bryan Cook signed with Cincinnati. The other pieces that left weren’t exactly overly significant with perhaps the exception of Isiah Pacheco and maybe Hollywood Brown. KANSAS CITY CHIEFS WIDE RECEIVER RASHEE RICE IS ON PACE FOR AN ALL-TIME FUMBLING OF THE BAG Roster After years of a great offense, the team switched to a great defense. Now, they seem to have reinvested in their offense. The unit gains dynamic balance with the backfield addition of Kenneth Walker III alongside Rashee Rice and Travis Kelce in the passing attack. The primary variable remains Mahomes' availability this season. Defensively, Steve Spagnuolo’s front seven remains formidable, anchored by Chris Jones and Creed Humphrey controlling the line of scrimmage. It will be interesting to see where the secondary improves from last year’s issues. They don’t have superstar-level players, but Spagnuolo is known to make the most out of his teams. CHIEFS LEGEND NOT READY TO SAY DYNASTY IS OVER DESPITE PATRICK MAHOMES' INJURY, TRAVIS KELCE'S FINAL DAYS Betting Outlook The Chiefs are a public team. They have the most well-known quarterback and tight end in the game. They are also a well-coached squad. They went 6-11 last season and as mentioned, lost a lot of close games. This year, the books have them listed at 10.5 games, and I just don’t see them getting to 11. It is hard to count them out, but Mahomes is coming off an ACL tear, the team has a lot of changes, and the division has gotten better with the Chargers and Broncos both looking like better teams. I’m going to avoid anything on the Chiefs, but I’d take the under 10.5 on them if I had to play anything. articles.title: Arizona Cardinals trade for Jacksonville Jaguars TE Hunter Long
articles.summary: The Cardinals bolster their tight end room with a former Rams tight end.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals had made another trade. After sending running back Corey Kiner to the New England Patriots, they have acquired a tight end. According to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport, they traded for Jacksonville Jaguars tight end Hunter Long.

Long is entering his sixth NFL season. He spent two years with the Miami Dolphins , who drafted him in the third round in 2021. He spent 2023-2024 with the Los Angeles Rams , where he crossed paths with Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur, who was the Rams' offensive coordinator both years Long was there.

He had 12 receptions for 85 yards and two touchdowns for the Jaguars last season. He is under contract through 2026 and will make $2 million in salary, $1 million of which is guaranteed.

Long has played all 17 games in a season only once — in 2024.

With Tip Reiman expected to start the season on the PUP reserve, Long gives the Cardinals a proven blocking tight end.

The terms of the trade were not immediately reported.

articles.title: Former Bills linebacker cut after career-high 129 tackles with Dolphins
articles.summary: Former Buffalo Bills linebacker Tyrel Dodson was released by the Miami Dolphins after recording career highs of 129 tackles and five sacks in 2025.
articles.body:
Tyrel Dodson just had the best season of his NFL career.

Now the former Buffalo Bills linebacker is looking for a job.

The Miami Dolphins are releasing Dodson despite the 28-year-old starting 16 games last season and recording career highs of 129 tackles and five sacks along with an interception and fumble recovery.

The move comes one year after Miami re-signed Dodson to a two-year, $8.25 million contract.

Dodson began his NFL career with Buffalo, signing with the Bills as an undrafted free agent out of Texas A&M in 2019.

Dodson spent five years with the Bills, appearing in 59 games with 15 starts. He competed with Terrel Bernard for the starting middle linebacker job in 2023 before Bernard won the role, but Dodson eventually started 10 games after Matt Milano suffered a season-ending leg injury.

Dodson finished that season with 74 tackles, 2.5 sacks and a forced fumble. Pro Football Focus named him the Bills' most improved player and gave him a 90.2 grade, best among NFL linebackers.

Dodson left Buffalo in free agency and signed with Seattle in 2024. The Seahawks surprisingly released him midway through that season despite Dodson starting all nine games and leading the team with 71 tackles.

Miami claimed him off waivers the next day.

Dodson made an immediate impact for the Dolphins, recording three interceptions in eight games to finish the 2024 season. He had 15 tackles and an interception against Cleveland in Week 17 and was named AFC Defensive Player of the Week.

That performance helped earn Dodson another contract with Miami, and he followed it with his most productive NFL season in 2025. He finished second on the Dolphins in tackles and third in sacks.

Dodson has now been released twice in less than two years despite being a productive starter both times.
